**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Buffer leading whitespace until text arrives**

When an output starts with a whitespace-only delta (for example, a response whose first chunk is `"\n"`), this newly admitted branch emits it immediately. `Assistant::Builtin` forwards the event to `AssistantMessage#append_text!`; that claims the pending message as `complete` and calls `save!`, but `Message` validates `content` with Rails presence, so whitespace-only content is rejected and the whole assistant turn enters the error path before later text can stream. Preserve the chunk by buffering it until a nonblank delta rather than emitting it as the first append.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**Correctness**: this now lets a leading whitespace-only chunk reach `Assistant::Builtin#respond_to`'s `on(:output_text)` handler, which can crash the whole turn rather than just costing a redundant transaction.

Trace: `assistant_message` starts `content: ""`, status `pending`. On the first `output_text` chunk, `assistant_message.content.blank?` is true, so `builtin.rb` enters the `Chat.transaction { assistant_message.append_text!(text); chat.update_latest_response!(...) }` branch. `AssistantMessage#append_text!` calls `claim!` first (since the message is still `pending`), which does `update_all(status: "complete")` — a raw SQL update that bypasses validations — then sets `self.status = :complete` in memory. It then does `self.content += text; save!`. `Message` validates `content` presence `unless: :pending?`; the message is no longer pending, so if `text` is whitespace-only (e.g. a lone `" "` chunk — exactly the case this PR is fixing), `content` is `" "`, which is `.blank?`, so `save!` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid`.

That exception propagates out of the `on(:output_text)` callback, through `responder.respond`, and into `respond_to`'s top-level `rescue => e`. There, `assistant_message.content.blank?` is still true (the in-memory `content` is `" "`), so the already-`complete`-flagged, now-invalid message is destroyed and `chat.add_error(e)` reports a failure — i.e. a response whose very first streamed chunk is pure whitespace now errors out the whole turn instead of streaming normally.

Might be worth having `Assistant::Builtin`'s first-chunk detection use something other than `content.blank?` (e.g. an explicit "has anything been appended yet" flag), or having `append_text!`/`claim!` tolerate a leading blank append without immediately validating presence.

_Single-pass review without the Agent tool (medium effort); traced against `app/models/assistant/builtin.rb`, `app/models/assistant_message.rb` and `app/models/message.rb` on `main`, which this PR doesn't touch._

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Yes, Codex was right: a response whose first streamed chunk is whitespace-only would have reached `Builtin#respond_to` with blank content and failed `save!` presence validation, which your Correctness trace below confirms. The underlying report (#4441) is real too: OpenAI streams the space before a number as its own chunk, so the old `present?` filter dropped it (`as of10-22-2026`).

Pushed a follow-up commit that holds leading whitespace back and emits it together with the first non-blank chunk, with a regression test for a stream that starts with `"\n"`, `" "`, `"Hello"`. The PR was prepared with Claude Code.

Thanks for the trace, it is accurate. Fixed in the new commit: `Assistant::Responder` now buffers leading whitespace-only chunks and emits them joined to the first non-blank chunk, so `Builtin` never sees a whitespace-only first append (no change needed in `builtin.rb`). Whitespace chunks after the first text still pass through, so `"as"`, `" of"`, `" "`, `"10"` still joins correctly. Added a test for a stream that starts with `"\n"`, `" "` then `"Hello"`.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Preserve buffered whitespace across tool rounds.** If one round emits `"as"` and a tool call, the next emits `" "` and another tool call, and the final round emits `"10"`, the output becomes `"as10"`. Each `request_response` discards its whitespace buffer when it returns. Provider responses can contain both text and tool calls. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/we-promise/sure/3c1f87df1009f9f3ae5f3517d1d338fd300765a8/app/models/provider/anthropic.rb)) Keep the buffer and first-emission state for the entire `respond` call. Keep per-response text detection separate.
